updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Cost is FLOP-proportional for group-3 width (E117), depth (E123) and the late freeze (E116, once group-2 conv1's dgrad is counted). It is not FLOP-proportional for narrow group-2 widths (E080: 33-60% recovered) or for pool and activation ops (E052, E023). A joint FLOP + byte cost model is untested (new cost-model node, H2.21.3). Tip: E116/E119 code, ~4.26 s, population mean 0.7521. Measured yardstick (E128): ~1 pp per 32 px epoch, ~0.05 pp per 1% of time. Measured lever rates in pp per 1%: 85% freeze ~0.02; 92->85% marginal ~0.035; depth 2/3/3 ~0.04 (E127); group-2 late freeze ~0.055 (E125); bs-1536 late revert ~0.085 (E126, a bad trade). Live levers: earlier freeze (75-80%), FreezeOut BN-eval, 3/3/2, group-3 width 512, early bs 2048, 16 px trim, 12 px, lookahead removal, and a funded combination with 32 px re-spend. Closed: CUDA graphs, Inductor tuning, cuDNN determinism/benchmark_limit, prepare, group-2 width, whitening-bias freeze point, 28 px substitution, bs-1536 late revert, group-2 late freeze, freeze LR anneal.
updates.reason: Stale lever list (review). E126 refuted the bs-1536 revert, and E128 measured the 32 px slope. E125 and E129 closed two freeze refinements. The FLOP-proportional claim is narrowed to where it was measured, and the rest is handed to a falsifiable cost model.

updates.statement: The local yardstick is now measured on the tip (E128, 100 seeds per arm). A 32 px phase change of -0.25 / +0.25 epoch gave -0.25 / +0.24 pp: ~1 pp per 32 px epoch, ~0.05 pp per 1% of time, symmetric. Every time lever is judged against this rate, both as a pure cut and as cut plus 32 px re-spend. Low-res trims have never been measured at large seed (see the 16 px trim under H8). Equal-time low-res/high-res reshuffles are null (E114).
updates.reason: E128 measured the slope at 100 seeds per arm, symmetric and inside H2.10.6's predicted band.
E128: -0.25 pp / +0.24 pp for -/+0.25 epoch at 32 px is ~0.05 pp per 1%, inside the predicted 0.03-0.07 band and symmetric.

updates.statement: Per-phase batch size matters only in the late phases. The bs-1024 28/32 px phases are a real purchase: E126 (100 seeds) shows bs 1536 there costs -0.18 pp for -2.1% time, ~0.085 pp per 1%, above the 0.05 yardstick. Low-res batch size is accuracy-neutral at fixed warmup (E121, +0.004 pp). Open: bs 2048 at 16/24 px with warmup fixed in steps (H2.11.7; E043's -0.49 pp is 3-seed and warmup-confounded), and smaller late batches (H2.11.5). This contradicts gradient-noise-scale theory, which says late training tolerates larger batches (search 1812.06162). The mechanism (update count vs EMA-window samples vs SGD rescale) is unconfirmed; see the E126 ablation under H11.2.
updates.reason: The review flagged 'reverting is the most likely free time lever' as stale: E126 refuted it at ~5 SE. Combined with E121, batch size matters by placement.

E126 is the 100-seed reverse of this test: bs 1536 at 28/32 px costs 0.18 pp, ~0.085 pp per 1%. That supports the claimed late-phase update gain and rate (>=0.055 pp per 1%), which the earlier E084/E085 runs could not resolve.

updates.statement: Un-retired. Its retirement premise (added steps are worth ~0.04 pp per 1% wherever they go, E104) was refuted by E121 vs E126. Late steps are worth ~0.085 pp per 1%. Step 1, untimed: profile bs 768 and 896 at 28/32 px (static, warmed) and project total time; bs 768 at 32 px is 54 M-tiles, ~2.5 waves on 108 SMs. Step 2: 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline, with bs 768 in the last ~1 epoch of the 32 px phase (sample-indexed; final-EMA/lookahead pinned to the last 8 steps; SGD groups kilostep-scaled; Muon unchanged). Prediction: gain >=+0.08 pp at <=+2.5% time, i.e. >=0.05 pp per 1%. If the gain is <=0.03 pp, the late-update effect saturates at bs 1024.
updates.reason: Review: the reason it was retired no longer holds after E121/E126, and search notes theory does not exclude it.
E126 (100 seeds): -0.18 pp vs E116 on the same seeds for -2.1% time. The predicted loss was <=0.05 pp, so the bs-1024 tail was a real purchase.

updates.statement: On the tip, run the 16/24 px phases at bs 2048 with the LR warmup fixed in steps, not samples (removes E043's warmup confound). SGD groups are kilostep-scaled; Muon is unchanged; all bs-2048 shapes and whiten-bias-grad variants are warmed in build. Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction (H8 early-threshold view, E121): time about -1% and a loss <=0.03 pp. If the loss is >=0.1 pp, large early batches hurt through a channel other than update count (e.g. fewer early steps under the SGD-bias warmup).
updates.reason: E121 showed early update count is worthless, which raises the prior that a larger early batch is free. The test is now also a prediction of the restated H8.

updates.statement: Depth cuts are FLOP-proportional time levers. E123 projected -7.6% for 2/3/3 and -6.1% for 3/3/2; E127 scored -7.0% for 2/3/3. Accuracy: 2/3/3 cost -0.29 pp at 100 seeds, ~0.04 pp per 1%, just under the 0.05 yardstick (E128). Re-spent on 32 px epochs at ~1 pp/epoch (~0.29 epoch, ~0.27 s), it nets only ~-0.7%, which is within error. The E127 post-mortem used 0.5 pp/epoch; the measured slope is ~1. 3/3/2 has no accuracy test yet. Weak outside support: airbench uses 2 convs per block in every short recipe and 3 only at 40 epochs (search).
updates.reason: Corrected the arithmetic with E128's slope (review), added E127's outcome, and noted the untested 3/3/2 arm.

updates.statement: Arm (a) 2/3/3 on the E116 base, untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Outcome E127: -0.29 pp for -7.0% scored time (~0.04 pp per 1%), between the 0.25 and 0.4 pp bars. As a funded variant (re-spend ~0.29 epoch at 32 px) it nets ~-0.7%, inside error. Arm (b) 3/3/2 moves to its own node.
updates.reason: E127 lands between the bars, and arm (b) never ran. Split so the 3/3/2 test is explicit.

Search (MosaicML stochastic-depth card) advises avoiding stochastic depth, or using a small drop rate, in nets with few blocks. The tip has 2 residual convs per group, and its gate (hard cut too costly) is ambiguous after E127.

updates.statement: On the E116 base, set group-3 width to 512 (head [100, 512], Muon stacks re-batched, all freeze x renorm variants warmed). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Bar from the measured yardstick (E128): -5.2% x 0.05 = 0.26 pp. Prediction: loss <=0.18 pp. If the loss is >=0.26 pp, the cut trades no better than a 32 px trim and group-3 width closes. Low prior: futurebiohackers chose 576 because late width buys CIFAR-100 accuracy (E005).
updates.reason: Bar updated from the assumed 0.035 slope to the measured 0.05 (E128). Still untested (review).

updates.statement: Late layer freezing is a real rate lever with a small, real accuracy cost. Stem + group 1 frozen from 85% of samples: -4.5% time, -0.09 pp (E118, 198 trajectories), banked (E119). From 92%: -2.5%, -0.02 pp (E120). Both trade below the 0.05 pp per 1% yardstick (E128); the 92->85 marginal rate is ~0.035. Closed refinements: freezing group 2 as well (E125: -0.18 pp, ~0.055 pp per 1%) and a FreezeOut LR anneal before the freeze (E129: +0.002 pp, the loss is not from abruptness). Open: the 75-80% points, BN eval mode in the frozen window (FreezeOut's own design, search), and progressive freeze (low prior).
updates.reason: Folded in E125 and E129 (both 100-seed refutations), and search support for the BN-eval arm.

updates.statement: Dose-response of the stem + group-1 freeze. Measured: 92% -0.02 pp / -2.5% (E120); 85% -0.09 pp / -4.5% (E118). Remaining: 80% and 75% of samples, untimed, 100 seeds each vs the pooled E100/E116 baselines, with per-trial times from one scored row each (every freeze x renorm variant warmed; TORCH_LOGS=recompiles dev check). Prediction: 80% saves ~5.5% at <=0.18 pp; 75% saves ~6.5% at <=0.30 pp. The 85->75 marginal rate must stay <=0.05 pp per 1% for an earlier freeze to beat 32 px re-spend. If the marginal rate is >0.06, the freeze stays at 85%.
updates.reason: The 75% point never ran (review). It decides whether the freeze can fund 32 px re-spend (frontier node).
E129 showed the freeze cost is not from abruptness, which removes the main rationale for a soft or stochastic freeze.
E125 (100 seeds): adding a group-2 freeze from 92% cost an extra -0.18 pp (predicted <=0.06) for -3.4%, ~0.055 pp per 1%. Late-freeze depth is capped at group 1.

updates.statement: FreezeOut-style refinement of the 85% freeze, arm (a): anneal the group-1 and stem-BN LRs to 0 over 75-85% of samples before the detach. Outcome E129: +0.002 pp vs E116 at 100 seeds. Refuted. Arm (b), BN eval mode in the frozen window, was never run and moves to its own node.
updates.reason: E129 is a clean 100-seed null for arm (a), against a predicted +0.04 pp recovery.
No new evidence. Raised in priority: it is untimed and gates the cost-model node and the early-downsampling stem idea (review).

updates.statement: Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and decisions near the gate select for luck. Single-component model (E113, one calibration pair): fp-level differences fully decorrelate a seed's trajectory. Per-trajectory sd ~0.26 pp, with no persistent seed component (paired sd 0.36 = sqrt(2) x 0.26). Expected sds: 3-seed scored mean ~0.15 pp; 100-seed mean ~0.026 pp; two-arm SE = 0.26*sqrt(1/nA+1/nB). Consequences: (1) 8-22-seed deltas of ~0.1 pp are noise (E104 vs E121). (2) Gate passes are population margin plus luck. The banked E116 code (population 0.7521) passes with p ≈ Phi((0.7521-0.753)/0.15) ≈ 27%. Its scored rows E116/E118/E119/E121/E122/E123*/E128 are 0.7501/0.7520/0.7531/0.7516/0.7505/0.7516/0.7533: 2 of 7 pass, mean 0.7517, consistent with the model. *E123's provenance is unresolved: its idea says it reran E090, but its time matches E116 (H4.2.4). (3) The official 40-seed mean has sd ~0.04 pp, so a population mean >= ~0.7513 clears 0.75 almost surely. (4) Margin is gone, so further accuracy-costing cuts must be funded. Open hint: E100's 5 distinct scored rows average 0.7543 vs its 0.7530 population (~2 SE), a possible recipe x seeds 0-2 offset (H4.9.1).
updates.reason: Fixed the gate tally (the review found the '1 of 6, ~45%' figure wrong: E119 and E128 both pass). Flagged E123's provenance and the single-pair basis of the noise model.
Still undone. First priority: resolve E123's source hash, because it is counted as a tip gate sample (review).

updates.statement: Acceptance rule. The 0.7518 floor was set post hoc, 0.0003 below the candidate it banked. First-principles replacement, pre-registered and not adjusted per candidate: (1) official safety: population mean mu >= 0.7513 on >=100 trajectories, i.e. >=3 sd of the 40-seed mean above 0.75; (2) local gate: at most 3 scored attempts, stopping at the first row >=0.753; (3) every banked time is reported with its pass probability Phi((mu-0.753)/0.15) and its observed pass count (E116 code: ~27%, 2/7). Margin-spending policy: a cut may lower mu only down to 0.7513, and each cut is accepted only if it trades below the 0.05 pp per 1% yardstick or is funded. A retry budget never substitutes for margin in the analysis.
updates.reason: The review showed the floor was tailored to E116 and that the headline time hides a ~27% pass rate. The rule is restated from the official bar and the local gate.

updates.statement: Free check on existing logs. For each same-code family with >=3 distinct scored samples and a >=100-trajectory population mean (E100: scored 0.7561/0.7516/0.7551/0.7532/0.7553/0.7534..., population 0.7530; E116: 7 rows, mean 0.7517, population 0.7521), plus the E090 family with its 22-seed mean, test whether the scored mean minus the population mean is within 2*0.15/sqrt(n) and whether the pass fraction matches Phi. Prediction: no family deviates by more than 2 SE. If E100's +0.13 pp gap (~2 SE) recurs with a consistent sign across families, add a per-recipe seeds-0-2 offset term to the gate model.
updates.reason: Updated with E116-family numbers. Still unrun and free (review).

updates.statement: The early phase is threshold-like. It needs a minimum resolution and exposure to form stem and group-1 features: removing the 24 px bridge cost -0.68 pp (E032), a 20 px bridge -0.38 pp (E041), and freezing the whitening bias at ~3% of samples -0.44 pp (E093). Beyond that minimum, marginal early updates are worthless (E121, 100 seeds: +0.004 pp). Low-res samples still carry some value: E114's null swap implies a 24 px epoch is worth ~0.5 pp, offsetting a 0.25-epoch 32 px cut. So the threshold applies to update count, not to sample exposure. Falsifiable predictions: early bs 2048 with step-fixed warmup is null (H2.11.7), and trimming 16 px samples (the cheapest, lowest-information phase) costs well under the 0.05 pp per 1% yardstick.
updates.reason: Review: no Lvl1 explained the early/late asymmetry. The old 'flat optimum' text is restated as a mechanism with predictions, consistent with E114 and E121.
E114 (100 seeds): moving 0.25 epoch of 32 px into 0.5 epoch of 24 px gave +0.02 pp (SE 0.033). The 24 px bridge does not buy accuracy at a better rate per unit time than the 32 px phase.
The 22-seed +0.09 pp (E108) did not replicate at 100 seeds (E114: +0.02), below the >= +0.1 pp prediction.
E114: +0.02 pp, ~1.8 SE below the predicted >=+0.08. The H8.2 side fails. The H11 rival threshold (<=-0.05) was not met either, so equal-time reallocation is neutral.

updates.statement: (Placement-independent form) Adding optimizer updates (smaller batches) at fixed epochs raises accuracy at a uniform ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% of time wherever they go. Refuted at 100 seeds: extra early updates gave +0.004 pp (E121), while late updates are worth ~0.18 pp per 2.1% (E126, reverse direction). Larger phase-local Muon lr is also null (E107, E110, E111). The placement-dependent version lives under H11.2.
updates.reason: Review: the refutation was read as global, but E126 shows late updates matter. The refutation is narrowed to placement independence.
Placement independence is directly refuted at 100 seeds: early steps +0.004 pp (E121) vs late steps ~0.18 pp (E126).

updates.statement: (Narrowed, reopened) Accuracy at the tip is bounded by late full-resolution training: fresh 28/32 px samples x updates in the final phases. Marginal low-res steps add nothing. 100-seed evidence: removing late updates (bs 1536 at 28/32 px) -0.18 pp (E126; confounded by EMA-window samples, SGD rescale and Muon path length); extra early updates +0.00 (E121); duplicated 32 px images -0.82 pp (E124); 32 px epochs ±1 pp per epoch (E128). Not supporting: late Muon lr (path length) is null at population level (E100/E110/E111), and an equal-time 24/32 px swap is null (E114), so exposure to the 32 px resolution itself is not uniquely binding. The binding quantity is late fresh samples and updates, not path length or resolution alone.
updates.reason: Review: it was retired on 22-seed evidence (E104, E108) that E121 and E114 have since removed. E121, E124, E126 and E128 at 100 seeds fit a late-binding mechanism.

updates.statement: Placement of updates. Added steps at low resolution buy nothing (E121, +0.004 pp at 100 seeds), while late 28/32 px steps are worth ~0.18 pp for ~2.1% time (E126, at ~5 SE). Caveat: E126 changes three things besides step count: the last-8-step EMA/lookahead window covers 1.5x more samples (E081 showed longer windows hurt), the SGD groups are kilostep-rescaled, and Muon path length falls by 1/3. The confound ablation decides whether update count is the mechanism.
updates.reason: The direct 100-seed contrast (E121 vs E126) matches this node's prediction. Not higher confidence because of E126's confounds (review).
E121 is the 100-seed version of this test: +0.004 pp for ~53 added low-res steps, inside the predicted <=+0.03. The E104 +0.12 that leaned against it was 22-seed noise.

Search: airbench94_muon, the source of the tip's Muon settings, and hiverge's Muon record use no lookahead or EMA. That lowers the prior that averaging strength is a live accuracy source under Muon. The deciding test is still the 100-seed removal (H9.2.2).
Premise test H9.2.2 is not yet run. Search lowers the prior that lookahead carries >=0.1 pp under Muon.
Search: neither Muon reference recipe uses lookahead or EMA, which lowers the prior for the predicted >=0.1 pp loss. A null result banks ~0.4% time. Rank this first among the zero-time audits.
Search: airbench uses translate 4 and cutout only in its 40-45-epoch recipes, and every <=15-epoch recipe uses translate 2. Lower prior.
Same as H12.3. Low priority.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~7-8 epochs, and Muon was the lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020), large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Closed: momentum, NS count, cheaper orthogonalizers, Muon lr in every phase (E105, E107, E110, E111), and a freeze LR anneal (E129). The head on Muon and head lr 0.5x are kept because they are free, but their gains are noise-level; a population-level audit is pending. New outside lead (search 2609.09676): Muon-C orthogonalizes each 3x3-DFT frequency block of a conv kernel instead of the unfolded matrix. It reports +0.4-0.6 pp over unfolded Muon on ImageNet-100, with gains concentrated early and on short budgets, but costs ~3.7x the NS FLOPs (own estimate). Open, low prior: schedule shape (H7.4), NorMuon (H7.5), Muon-C.
updates.reason: Added the only outside accuracy lead from search and noted the pending audit of the head components.

new.statement: Per-step time at a given (resolution, batch) shape is predicted by a two-term model, t = a·conv FLOPs + b·bytes moved by the BN/GELU forward and backward, fit per resolution on existing profiles (E080 group-2 widths, E117 group-3 widths, E122 per-group backward, E123 depth). This falsifiable model replaces H2's 'FLOP-proportional except...' clause. A clearly positive b means byte levers at high resolution (stem/group 1) trade better than FLOP-equivalent cuts.

Free/untimed: fit a and b on the >=8 per-step variants already profiled (E080, E117, E123), per resolution. Prediction: residuals <=3% on the fit set. Out of sample, the model predicts E116's frozen 32 px / bs-1024 step and E127's 2/3/3 step within ±3%. If b ≈ 0, H2.21's byte claim is refuted. If residuals exceed 5% for group-2 widths, a tile-quantization term is needed.

Levers that trade below the 0.05 pp per 1% yardstick (85% freeze ~0.02, 92->85 marginal ~0.035, possibly 2/3/3 at ~0.04 and the untested 3/3/2 / early bs 2048 / 16 px trim) can be combined with 32 px re-spend (~1 pp per epoch, E128) for a net time gain at constant population mean. The tree has so far judged each lever only as a pure cut against a fixed margin.

After the 75/80% freeze points, 3/3/2, early bs 2048 and the 16 px trim are measured at 100 seeds, build one candidate. Include every lever measured at <=0.045 pp per 1%, then add 32 px epochs (sample-indexed, freeze point rescaled) until the predicted mean is back at the tip's 0.7521. Pre-register the predicted time from the measured rates (sum of savings minus re-spend at ~0.89 s per 32 px epoch, adjusted for the frozen fraction). Prediction: time >=1.5% below 4.262 s, with a 100-seed mean within 0.03 pp of 0.7521. If the measured net saving is <0.5%, or the mean falls >0.06 pp short of prediction, lever rates do not add (interactions) and the frontier line closes.

Arm (b) 3/3/2 on the E116 base: drop group-3 conv3, re-batch the Muon stacks, warm every freeze x renorm x whiten-bias-grad variant, and confirm no recompiles on a 2-trial dev run. Untimed per-step profile with the freeze on, then 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction: projected saving >=5%, and loss <=0.20 pp, well under the ~0.30 pp bar at 0.05 pp per 1%. If the loss is >=0.30 pp, depth cuts close.

FreezeOut arm (b). In the frozen window (85% of samples onward), run stem + group-1 BN in eval mode using the running stats at freeze time, as a separate warmed static graph variant. This removes the batch-stat reductions over the 31x31x128 activations. Untimed per-step profile plus 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction: time -0.2% to -0.5%, loss <=0.02 pp. If the loss is >=0.05 pp, the frozen layers' train-mode BN still adapts usefully to the shifting downstream input, and the line closes.

Gated on H2.21.3 or N_costmodel showing stem/group-1 bytes cost >=1.2x their FLOP share. Untimed profile of a cheaper early stage: move group 1's max-pool from after conv3 to after conv1, so conv2/conv3 run at 15x15 instead of 31x31. Warm all shapes, freeze variants included. Prediction: projected saving >=8%. Score at 100 seeds only if it is >=8%, with the bar at 0.05 pp per 1%. Low prior: early high-resolution capacity was fragile (E093, E032).

Confound ablation of E126, untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. On the tip, run the 28/32 px phases at bs 1536, but pin the final-EMA window and lookahead stop to the same sample count as the tip (~8192 samples, ~5 steps) and keep the SGD groups at their bs-1024 values (no kilostep rescale). Muon x1.25 is unchanged. All bs-1536 freeze x renorm variants are warmed. Prediction (update-count mechanism): loss >=0.12 pp, reproducing most of E126's -0.18. If the loss is <=0.05 pp, E126 came from the window or SGD rescale, and both H11.2 and H2.11.5 lose their basis.

Early-phase threshold mechanism. After the 24 px bridge and the whitening-bias window (~41% of samples), early features are formed, and further low-res samples or updates have low marginal value per unit time. 16 px samples are the least informative, so they are the cheapest to remove.

On the tip, trim the 16 px phase from 2.0 to 1.5 epochs: sample-indexed switches, with LR warmup/decay, floor-hold, renorm cadence, whitening-bias window and the 85% freeze all rescaled to the new total; all shapes already warmed. Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction: time about -3% (0.5 x ~0.26 s) and loss <=0.05 pp, i.e. <=0.017 pp per 1%, far below the yardstick. If the loss is >=0.15 pp (>=0.05 pp per 1%), the threshold view is wrong for 16 px exposure.

Muon-C: orthogonalizing each frequency block of the 3x3-DFT of the kernel momentum, instead of the unfolded [Cout, 9*Cin] matrix, gives better-conditioned conv updates. Gains are concentrated early and on short budgets (+0.4-0.6 pp ImageNet-100 top-1 over unfolded Muon; same quality at 0.62x FLOPs). Risk: ~3.7x the NS FLOPs (1 real block + 4 conjugate pairs as 2Cout x 2Cin real matrices; own estimate), and the paper's fp32 5-step NS must be ported to bf16 with 3 steps.

Step 1, untimed: implement Muon-C in the compiled batched update (bf16, 3 NS steps, frequency blocks batched per shape) and measure ms/step vs the current update at 16 and 24 px. Step 2, only if the added time for the 16/24 px phases is <=+3% of the run: apply it to the group filters in the 16/24 px phases only (unfolded Muon at 28/32 px), 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction: gain >=+0.15 pp, and >=0.05 pp per 1% of added time. If the gain is <=0.05 pp, the CIFAR-100 short-budget benefit does not transfer and the line closes.

Zero-time tip components were adopted on <=1.5 SE evidence: head on Muon and head lr 0.5x (E044 one run, E062/E063), Muon x1.25 at 32 px (E100, null at population level), the pinned 8-step window (E096), the Fable tail's floor-hold and final EMA (E068/E069; E079 8-seed), and lookahead (E092 8-seed). At least one of them is null and costs time, or is slightly harmful. 100-seed removal ablations against the pooled E116 baseline can recover >=0.08 pp of margin, or ~0.4% time, at zero accuracy cost. Low-moderate prior: most of these were neutral-to-positive in their noisy tests, but the Muon reference recipes use no lookahead/EMA (search).
The optimizer-side scalars on the head and in the 32 px phase (head on Muon, head lr 0.5x, Muon x1.25 at 32 px) were never compared at population level. One of them costs >=0.08 pp.

On E116 code, run three untimed arms of 100 seeds each vs the pooled E116 baseline: (a) head Muon lr 1x instead of 0.5x; (b) Muon factor 1.0 instead of 1.25 at 32 px; (c) head weight back on SGD with the pre-E044 settings. All changes are 0-d tensors or warmed variants, so nothing recompiles. Prediction: at least one arm gains >=+0.08 pp (~2.4 SE vs pooled); that removal is adopted as margin. If all three are within ±0.05 pp, the components are neutral and stay for simplicity of lineage.

On E116 code, remove only the final 8-step EMA: evaluate on the net weights and keep the floor-hold and lookahead stop. Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction (H9 premise, E079's 8-seed -0.18): loss >=0.1 pp. If the loss is <=0.04 pp, the final EMA is null at population level. Together with a null H9.2.2, averaging strength is then closed and H9 is retired.
